resources.name: Crucial Music
resources.description: Non-exclusive sync agency with personalized service. 50/50 sync fee split; you keep 100% writer royalties. Must own masters and be registered with a PRO.

resources.name: Bodega Sync
resources.description: Division of Symphonic Distribution. Curated roster of indie artists/labels with 30+ years experience. Pre-cleared catalog for one-stop licensing. Note: requires a 2-year exclusive contract with 30% commission and does not register songs with PROs.

resources.name: TAXI
resources.description: Established in 1992. Publishes screened music-wanted listings from supervisors, labels, ad agencies, and game companies. Screeners review and forward qualifying tracks. Note: ~$300/year + $5/submission with reported placement rates around 6%; valuable mostly for feedback rather than placements.

resources.name: Musicbed
resources.description: Premium placements with brands like Nike, Google, Netflix, Spotify. High-quality curated catalog for film and advertising.

resources.name: Marmoset
resources.description: Indie-focused, creative approach. Non-exclusive deals, typically 50/50 split. Has paid artists over $44M all-time.

resources.name: Audio Network
resources.description: One of the largest global sync libraries with 300,000+ tracks. Transparent pricing, broadcast-ready music. International roster.

resources.name: Jingle Punks
resources.description: Award-winning agency with offices in NYC, LA, Toronto, London. 400,000+ song library, 4,000+ artists. Exclusive contracts, 50/50 split. Note: not accepting new artist submissions as of September 2026.

resources.name: Nightingale Music
resources.description: 30+ years of experience. Custom pricing per project. Strong in Canadian and international productions. Personal support.

resources.name: Pond5
resources.description: One of the largest royalty-free media marketplaces (25M+ stock clips). Artists upload tracks and set their own prices. Composer note: 30% royalty cut per sale; contributor music has been used for AI training.
resources.cost: Free to upload; Pond5 takes 70% commission

resources.name: Artlist
resources.description: Subscription model for buyers. Curated catalog with high production standards. Popular with content creators and filmmakers. Note: not accepting music submissions as of September 2026.

resources.name: Epidemic Sound
resources.description: Artists receive upfront payments and revenue shares. 50/50 streaming royalty split plus access to a $4.2M annual Soundtrack Bonus pool. Composer note: Epidemic uses 100% buy-out contracts that have been formally denounced by the European Composer & Songwriter Alliance — composers transfer rights for the full term of protection and lose PRO royalties. Not accepting new artist applications as of September 2026.

resources.name: Jamendo
resources.description: Accessible platform for indie musicians. Free uploads, non-exclusive. Unlimited submissions. YouTube Content ID integration.

resources.name: Ditto Pro (Sync Dashboard)
resources.description: Ditto Pro subscribers access sync briefs across TV, film, and ad campaigns. Ditto reviews tracks and pitches on your behalf.

resources.name: Sync Money
resources.description: Leading online community for sync licensing. Provides insider knowledge, industry connections, and access to real opportunities. The newsletter is free and sends sync briefs that subscribers can submit to; no paid tiers are listed. The website and blog haven't been updated since April 2025. Focus on getting real opportunities for music makers in TV, Film, Advertising, Video Games.

resources.name: Nitrility
resources.description: Blockchain-powered music-licensing marketplace. Search, request, negotiate, and clear sync licenses for songs from a 200-million-song catalog. Trusted by 80,000+ artists, labels, and publishers. Features include AI-powered search, expert curation, automated notifications, contract handling, payments, and dispute protection. Signing up and browsing is completely free; license prices vary by rights-holder. ⚠️ Selling is still limited to a select test group of artists and labels, and the promised opening to all rights-holders has been pending since at least September 2025; until then, license requests for songs you own are forwarded to you, and rights-holders can email to ask about early-partner access.
resources.cost: Free to browse; license prices vary

resources.name: One Night Stand Music & Management
resources.description: Subscription-based sync licensing model. Direct pitching to film, TV, ads, gaming. Artists keep ownership of music and avoid losing rights. Zero commission on placements—flat $35/month subscription replaces commission model. Almost all opportunities are non-exclusive. Transparent, flexible approach focused on artist control.

resources.name: Music Vine
resources.description: Indie-friendly sync library with high-quality curation. Each track must be reviewed and approved. Artists need at least 50% exclusive catalog with platform. Revenue split: 60% on exclusive tracks, 35% on non-exclusive. Tailored for professional video and film creators who value exclusivity and quality. Known for high-quality curation and strong placement opportunities for independent composers. Artist applications are currently closed; Music Vine says it may reopen them but won't answer application inquiries until then.

resources.name: Millennial Mind Sync — Supervisor Directory
resources.description: 325+ music supervisors indexed with LinkedIn profiles, email contact methods, and project histories. Includes a free pitch email generator tool.

resources.name: SongwriterUniverse — Supervisors Directory
resources.description: Free list of music supervisors in the US, Canada, and UK with company names, addresses, and contact info.

resources.name: Guild of Music Supervisors
resources.description: Non-profit organization for music supervision professionals. News, events, and the GMS Awards; the member directory requires a login. Useful for researching who supervises what.
resources.cost: Free to browse; Friend of the Guild $100/yr

resources.name: Aristake — Sync Agents Guide
resources.description: Free guide listing sync agents and how to get music synced on TV, video games, and films.

resources.name: Musco Sound — Library Submission Guide
resources.description: Free guide with direct links to submit music to various tiers of sync libraries.

resources.name: IMDb / IMDb Pro
resources.description: Look up music supervisors by searching film/TV credits. IMDb Pro provides contact details and project history.

resources.name: The Sync Report
resources.description: 1,000+ music supervisors, music buyers, and ad agency contacts in USA, UK, Canada, and Australia. TV calendar for optimal pitch timing.

resources.name: Music Business Registry — Film & TV Music Guide
resources.description: Industry-standard directory for 30+ years. Thousands of listings with direct phone/email. Covers supervisors, studios, licensing execs, game companies.

resources.name: Underground Mix — Sync Library Submission List
resources.description: 120+ vetted sync libraries, micro-licensing sites, and music houses. Includes submission checklist and email pitch template. Created by former Extreme Music / Paramount / Sony professionals.

resources.name: Music Supervisors Directory
resources.description: Curated directory of music supervisor contacts in LA, NYC, London, Canada, and Australia. Updated monthly.

resources.name: Songtrust — Sync Crash Course
resources.description: Free crash course covering sync licensing fundamentals: deal structures, sync fees, rights, placement types, and royalty collection.

resources.name: The Sync Lab (Aaron Davison)
resources.description: Free 4-hour video course covering how to create sync-ready music, pitch effectively, and land placements. Includes a free licensing directory.

resources.name: Dark Horse Institute — Sync Guide
resources.description: Blog with strategies and tips for getting sync placements as an independent musician.

resources.name: Collabhouse — Demystifying Sync Licensing
resources.description: Guide explaining how sync licensing works as a revenue stream and exposure tool for independent artists.

resources.name: 2Indie — The Sync Society
resources.description: Private music licensing club. Weekly Zoom calls with industry professionals (sync agencies, supervisors, producers). Monthly curated sync sampler sent to agencies.

resources.name: Elite Music Coaching (Michael Elsner & Jody Friedman)
resources.description: Sync licensing training from producer Michael Elsner (3,000+ placements) and music supervisor Jody Friedman, formerly Master Music Licensing. Programs include the Sync Placement Academy course and the Sync Titan private members' community.

resources.name: Ari's Take Academy — Advanced Sync Strategies
resources.description: Course on sync licensing including how to get signed to agents. Includes showcases with top-tier sync agencies and direct submission opportunities. Enrollment opens periodically; between sessions, admission is by application.

resources.name: Sync My Music
resources.description: Free sync licensing course for producers covering creating licensable music, finding libraries, and building income through performance royalties. Paid memberships (Sync Academy, Sync Edge) add production tutorials and library recommendations.

resources.name: ThatPitch Blog
resources.description: Extensive articles on sync licensing opportunities, companies, fees, strategies, and trends.

resources.name: Millennial Mind Sync Blog
resources.description: Articles on sync libraries, music supervisors, submission strategies, and free tools (music supervisor pitch generator, beat pricing calculator). No new posts since February 2024.

resources.name: Stock Music Musician
resources.description: Blog focused on production music and sync library submissions with reviews and guides.

resources.name: The Sync Report Podcast
resources.description: Podcast connecting songwriters with the sync licensing industry. No new episodes since February 2023; the 47-episode archive is still available.

resources.name: Rareform Audio Blog
resources.description: Articles on how sync licensing empowers independent artists outside traditional label structures.
